Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks for the heads-up, and sorry for the confusion. We recreated the invites and attached two ICS files:
- demo_invite-Europe.ics (anchored to Europe/London, event body includes TZID and a full VTIMEZONE block)
- demo_invite-US.ics (anchored to America/Los_Angeles)

Why this should fix it: when an ICS lacks a VTIMEZONE block or only specifies a UTC offset, some calendar clients treat the time as "floating" (no anchor) and display it relative to the viewing calendar without applying daylight-savings corrections. Adding TZID/VTIMEZONE ensures Google Calendar, Outlook, and most clients interpret the time correctly.

Steps I took:
1) Generated two separate events pinned to the appropriate TZID (Europe/London and America/Los_Angeles).
2) Included the TZID string in the SUMMARY to make the local time visible at a glance.
3) Exported each event as a standalone .ics that contains the VTIMEZONE section.

Attachments: demo_invite-Europe.ics, demo_invite-US.ics

Please accept the Europe invite if youd like the 14:00 GMT / 15:00 CET slot. If you prefer a US anchor, use the US invite.

—Vivek
